# Step 1: Obtain Initial Metadata from Each Project

This step sets the project directory and loads the raw SRA metadata.

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Load libraries
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(cowplot)

# (1) Setting working directory
project_id <- "PRJNA1154284"

base_dir <- "E:/工作区/VSCode/RNAproject/collect_metadata_respon/project"
setwd(file.path(base_dir, project_id))

# (2) Loading raw SRA metadata file
sra_file <- "SraRunTable.csv"
initial_meta <- read.csv(sra_file, header = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
```

# Step 2: Data Overview

First, you need to get an overview of the data, which includes two steps: reading the article and reading the initial metadata. This step is very IMPORTANT!

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# (1) Read the article in the following order: abstract, the beginning of the results section, and the methods.
# Paper summary used for this project:
# - Title: Supragingival Plaque Microbiomes in a Diverse South Florida Population
# - Study design: oral-site matched sampling study in a diverse South Florida cohort with one participant sampled again one year later
# - Deposited sequencing rows: 135 total oral samples from 26 participants; 25 participants sampled once at five oral sites and one participant (FN54) sampled at the same five sites twice
# - Sample type for this metadata: four supragingival plaque quadrants plus tongue scrape
# - Participant eligibility in Methods: adults aged 18-40 years, South Florida residents, no active periodontal disease, and no antibiotic use in the last 3 months
# - Sequencing from Methods: 16S rRNA gene V4 region amplified with primers 515F and 806R and sequenced on Illumina MiSeq V3 600-cycle chemistry
# - Health groups from Table 1 / Results: periodontally healthy, localized gingivitis, generalized gingivitis
# - The paper reports 131 samples in downstream analyses because four deposited samples were omitted for low sequencing reads, but the SRA deposit contains 135 oral samples
# - Supplementary Materials mention Supplemental Table S1 with sequencing statistics; this is useful for checking the 131-vs-135 discrepancy, but it is not currently required as a join table for the 19-column metadata export

# (2) IMPORTANT: MUST go through each column of initial_meta
head(initial_meta, 10)
colnames(initial_meta)
table(initial_meta$Instrument)
table(initial_meta$isolation_source)
table(initial_meta$HOST)
table(initial_meta$geo_loc_name_country)
table(sub("-.*$", "", initial_meta$`Sample Name`))
table(sub(".*-", "", initial_meta$`Sample Name`))
table(initial_meta$ReleaseDate)
# Relevant raw-table overview for the 19-column export:
# - Already present in SRA: sample_id (Run), bioproject (BioProject), country (geo_loc_name_country), public_time (ReleaseDate), site clues (isolation_source, Sample Name), matched/cohort structure clues (Sample Name)
# - Must come from the paper: title, sequencing_region, platform, pcr_primers, disease_study, status, age, bmi, sex
# - Still needs manual confirmation from paper/supplement context rather than SRA alone: participant-level status labels, participant-level demographics, and whether any deposited rows should be excluded from analysis-only summaries but retained in metadata export
# Raw-table summary checked for this project:
# - All deposited rows are human oral amplicon samples from USA.
# - isolation_source separates 108 Plaque rows from 27 Tongue scrape rows.
# - Sample names follow subject-site format: FNxx-UR/UL/LR/LL/T.
# - FN54a and FN54b represent the same participant sampled at two timepoints one year apart.
# - SRA contains enough information to standardize sample_id, subject grouping, site, country, and release date, but not participant demographics or gingival-health status.
```

# Step 3: Removing Control and Non-human Samples

First, we need to remove control samples(including both negative controls and positive controls) and non-human samples.

```{r}
# (1) Parameter setup
control_column <- ""
control_keywords <- c()

species_column <- "HOST"
unique(initial_meta[[species_column]])
non_human_keywords <- c()

# (2) Remove controls and non-human samples. DO NOT need to modify code in this part, just run it.
n_samples <- nrow(initial_meta)
# Control evaluation
if (length(control_keywords) > 0) {
  if (is.null(control_column) || control_column == "") {
    stop("Error: control_keywords provided but control_column is missing.")
  }

  if (!(control_column %in% colnames(initial_meta))) {
    stop(sprintf("Error: Column '%s' not found in initial_meta.", control_column))
  }

  control_pattern <- paste(control_keywords, collapse = "|")
  control_text <- initial_meta[[control_column]]
  is_control <- grepl(control_pattern, control_text)

} else {
  is_control <- rep(FALSE, n_samples)
}

# Non-human evaluation
if (length(non_human_keywords) > 0) {
  if (is.null(species_column) || species_column == "") {
    stop("Error: non_human_keywords provided but species_column is missing.")
  }

  if (!(species_column %in% colnames(initial_meta))) {
    stop(sprintf("Error: Column '%s' not found in initial_meta.", species_column))
  }

  non_human_pattern <- paste(non_human_keywords, collapse = "|")
  species_text <- initial_meta[[species_column]]
  is_non_human <- grepl(non_human_pattern, species_text)
} else {
  is_non_human <- rep(FALSE, n_samples)
}

# Execute removal
samples_to_remove <- is_control | is_non_human
initial_meta <- initial_meta[!samples_to_remove, ]

cat("Initial samples counts:", n_samples, "\n")
cat("Removed control samples:", sum(is_control), "\n")
cat("Removed non-human samples:", sum(is_non_human), "\n")
cat("Total samples removed ", sum(samples_to_remove), "\n")
cat("Remaining samples after Step 2:", nrow(initial_meta), "\n")
```

# Step 4: Creating a Uniform Metadata Template

This step converts the raw SRA table into the standard metadata format used in our meta-analysis.

```{r}
raw_subject_code <- sub("-.*$", "", initial_meta$`Sample Name`)
subject_id <- sub("[ab]$", "", raw_subject_code)

# Table 1 contains participant-level age, BMI, sex, and gingival-health labels.
# The 26-row lookup table below transcribes those values once, then joins them to all site-level rows.
subject_info <- tibble::tribble(
  ~subject_id, ~age, ~bmi, ~sex, ~status,
  "FN02", 20, 34.15, "M", "HC",
  "FN08", 27, 25.80, "M", "localized gingivitis",
  "FN10", 27, 18.89, "F", "localized gingivitis",
  "FN11", 20, 25.10, "M", "HC",
  "FN13", 24, 25.39, "M", "HC",
  "FN16", 22, 33.90, "M", "localized gingivitis",
  "FN22", 20, 28.06, "M", "localized gingivitis",
  "FN24", 21, 23.13, "F", "generalized gingivitis",
  "FN25", 38, 30.43, "M", "HC",
  "FN26", 30, 44.24, "F", "HC",
  "FN27", 18, 24.41, "F", "HC",
  "FN31", 35, 20.45, "M", "HC",
  "FN32", 33, 21.14, "F", "localized gingivitis",
  "FN33", 30, 19.22, "M", "localized gingivitis",
  "FN34", 29, 24.39, "M", "HC",
  "FN35", 22, 21.41, "M", "HC",
  "FN36", 37, 28.15, "F", "HC",
  "FN37", 29, 21.11, "M", "generalized gingivitis",
  "FN39", 31, 21.28, "F", "HC",
  "FN40", 20, 24.03, "M", "HC",
  "FN43", 33, 20.36, "M", "HC",
  "FN47", 19, 22.31, "M", "HC",
  "FN50", 19, 23.17, "F", "HC",
  "FN52", 25, 36.02, "M", "HC",
  "FN54", 26, 54.24, "M", "HC",
  "FN71", 23, 20.17, "F", "HC"
)

metadata <- initial_meta %>%
  transmute(
    bioproject = BioProject,
    sample_id = Run,
    raw_subject_id = `Sample Name`,
    subject_id = subject_id,
    age = NA_real_,
    age_info = NA_character_,
    bmi = NA_real_,
    sex = NA_character_,
    sequencing_region = "V4",
    platform = "Illumina MiSeq",
    country = geo_loc_name_country,
    raw_site = isolation_source,
    site = ifelse(isolation_source == "Tongue scrape", "tongue dorsum", "supragingival plaque"),
    site_group = "pending",
    public_time = sub("T.*$", "", ReleaseDate),
    pcr_primers = "515F-806R",
    title = "Supragingival Plaque Microbiomes in a Diverse South Florida Population",
    disease_study = "yes",
    status = NA_character_,
    matched_samples = "pending",
    is_time_series = ifelse(grepl("^FN54[ab]$", raw_subject_code), "yes", "no")
  )

metadata <- metadata %>%
  left_join(subject_info, by = "subject_id", suffix = c("", ".subject")) %>%
  mutate(
    age = age.subject,
    bmi = bmi.subject,
    sex = sex.subject,
    status = status.subject
  ) %>%
  select(-age.subject, -bmi.subject, -sex.subject, -status.subject)

# Source notes for non-obvious fields:
# - raw_subject_id preserves the deposited Sample Name used to derive subject_id.
# - subject_id removes the oral-site suffix from Sample Name and also collapses FN54a/FN54b to FN54 because the paper states one participant was sampled twice one year apart.
# - age, bmi, sex, and status are mapped from paper Table 1 at the participant level, then propagated to all rows from that participant.
# - age_info is left as NA because exact participant ages are available from Table 1, so an approximate-age field is unnecessary.
# - country follows the SRA geo_loc_name_country field (USA); the paper gives the more specific recruitment geography South Florida, which is recorded here only in the evidence notes.
# - raw_site preserves the original SRA isolation_source values.
# - site uses the SRA isolation_source values together with the paper Methods: Tongue scrape is recorded as tongue dorsum, and plaque rows are standardized to supragingival plaque rather than keeping quadrant suffixes as separate exported site labels.
# - sequencing_region, platform, and pcr_primers come from the Methods section: V4 amplified with 515F/806R and sequenced on Illumina MiSeq V3 600-cycle chemistry.
# - disease_study is yes because the cohort includes localized and generalized gingivitis in addition to healthy participants.
# - The paper reports 131 samples in downstream analyses after low-read filtering, but all 135 deposited human oral SRA rows are retained in this metadata table.
# - is_time_series is yes only for FN54a/FN54b rows because the paper reports one participant sampled twice one year apart; all other repeated rows are matched oral-site samples rather than longitudinal follow-up.
metadata$public_time <- as.Date(metadata$public_time)
```

# Step 5: Manually solving pending issues

This step involves two parts: (1) handle the columns with the `raw_` prefix, and next (2) handle the `site_group` and `matched_samples` columns.

```{r}
# (1) raw_subject_id and raw_site are already carried in metadata to preserve the deposited Sample Name and isolation_source used for subject/site standardization.
metadata <- metadata
```

```{r}
# (2) Filling the 'site_group' and 'matched_samples' columns
unique(metadata$site)
Oral_site = c("supragingival plaque", "tongue dorsum")
Gut_site = c("feces")

metadata <- metadata %>%
  mutate(site_group = case_when(
    site %in% Oral_site ~ "oral",
    site %in% Gut_site ~ "gut",
    TRUE ~ "other"
  ))

metadata$matched_samples <- ifelse(
  ave(metadata$subject_id, metadata$subject_id, FUN = length) > 1,
  "yes",
  "no"
)
# matched_samples is yes because each participant contributes biologically matched oral samples across multiple sites in the same study design; FN54 additionally contributes a second visit one year later.
```

```{r}
# (3) check if there is pending value in metadata. If there is pending value, go on modify the metadata.
has_pending <- function(col) {
  if (is.character(col) || is.factor(col)) {
    any(col == "pending", na.rm = TRUE)
  } else {
    FALSE
  }
}

any_pending_value <- any(sapply(metadata, has_pending))

if (!any_pending_value) {
  message("Good! No cell contains the value 'pending'.")
} else {
  pending_cols <- names(metadata)[sapply(metadata, has_pending)]
  message("Columns containing 'pending': ", paste(pending_cols, collapse = ", "))
  message("Please continue to resolve these pending columns!")
}
```

# Step 6: Visualize the Metadata

This step makes a quick set of plots for checking the distribution of key metadata fields.

```{r}
plot_data <- metadata %>%
  select(-bioproject, -sample_id, -subject_id, -title)

create_simple_plots <- function(data) {
  plots <- list()
  continuous_vars <- c("age", "bmi")

  for (col in colnames(data)) {
    if (all(is.na(data[[col]]))) {
      p <- ggplot() +
        annotate("text", x = 0.5, y = 0.5, label = "this column is NA", size = 6) +
        labs(title = col) +
        theme_void()
    } else if (col %in% continuous_vars && is.numeric(data[[col]])) {
      p <- ggplot(data, aes(x = .data[[col]])) +
        geom_histogram(fill = "blue", alpha = 0.6, bins = 20, na.rm = TRUE) +
        labs(title = col, x = col, y = "Count") +
        theme_minimal()
    } else {
      count_data <- as.data.frame(table(data[[col]], useNA = "ifany"))
      p <- ggplot(count_data, aes(x = reorder(Var1, -Freq), y = Freq)) +
        geom_col(fill = "red", alpha = 0.6) +
        labs(title = col, x = NULL, y = "Count") +
        theme_minimal() +
        theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 15, hjust = 1))
    }
    plots[[col]] <- p
  }

  return(plots)
}

plots <- create_simple_plots(plot_data)
p <- plot_grid(plots$age,
               plots$bmi,
               plots$sex,
               plots$site,
               plots$site_group,
               plots$sequencing_region,
               plots$platform,
               plots$country,
               plots$status,
               plots$matched_samples,
               ncol = 3, align = "hv", axis = "lb")
ggsave("Metadata_Summary.png", plot = p, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 150)
```

```{r}
knitr::include_graphics("Metadata_Summary.png")
```

# Step 7: Sort and export the metadata

This step saves the cleaned metadata table as the final `metadata_v2.csv` file.

```{r}
fixed_cols <- c("bioproject", "sample_id", "subject_id", "age", "age_info",
                "bmi", "sex", "platform", "sequencing_region", "pcr_primers",
                "country", "site", "site_group", "disease_study", "status",
                "title", "public_time", "matched_samples", "is_time_series")
metadata <- metadata %>%
  select(all_of(fixed_cols), starts_with("raw_"))

write.csv(metadata, file = "metadata_v2.csv", quote = TRUE, row.names = FALSE)
```
